## Look through drug screen datasets

```{r}
# Load drug screen data 
load("data/drugscreen.Rda")

# use anyNA() function on data to see if any values are missing
anyNA(plate1)
anyNA(plate_meta)
anyNA(compound_dict)

# plate1 and plate_meta don't have any NA values 
# see how many NAs are in compound_dict
summary(compound_dict)
```

After looking through data, I can see that the plate maps for luminescence and compounds don't contain any NA values. compound_dict has one NA value (cmpd_6618, where it's hgnc symbol is not included). This information is useful going into analyses, as I don't have to remove NAs in the plate_meta and plate1 datasets.

# Question 1: Using the geom_tile() function, visualise the luminescence across the plate. Do there appear to be any spatial patterns in this data?

## Load packages

```{r}
# Load tidyverse and ggplot2
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)

```

## Prepare plate1 dataset to use geom_tile()

plate1 contains luminescence (RLU) values, and will therefore be used to answer Q1

```{r}
# geom_tile requires plate1 to be in long format

plate1_long <- plate1 |> 
  pivot_longer(
    # collapse all columns into 1 column except plate_row 
    cols = -plate_row, 
    # all columns collapsed into 1 column named "plate_col"
    names_to = "plate_col", 
    # all RLU values in column named "luminescence"
    values_to = "luminescence"
  )

# Check that pivot_longer() worked 
View(plate1_long)

# Convert plate_row and plate_col values from character to numeric 
# using parse_number() for 'tidier' data

plate1_long <- plate1_long |> 
  mutate(
    # keep numbers after "row"
    plate_row = parse_number(plate_row),
    # keep numbers after "col"
    plate_col = parse_number(plate_col))

# Check rows and columns have numeric values 
View(plate1_long)
```

## Visualise luminescence as heatmap

Loading esquisse

```{r}
# Install and load esquisse

remotes::install_github("dreamRs/esquisse")

library(esquisse)

esquisse::esquisser(plate1_long)
```

Copy/paste code from esquisse below:

```{r}
ggplot(plate1_long) +
  
  aes(x = plate_col, y = plate_row, fill = luminescence) +
  geom_tile(
    colour = "grey50", 
    linewidth = 0.1
  ) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "viridis", direction = 1) +
  # label every 2nd column number at the top to avoid over-cluttering
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1, 48, by = 2), expand = c(0, 0), position = "top") +
  # use scale_y_reverse() to get rows to start from 1 at the top like a plate
  scale_y_reverse(breaks = seq(1, 32, by = 2), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  coord_equal() +
  # add title, axes titles and legend
  labs(
    x = "Column",
    y = "Row",
    title = "Luminescence across 1536-well plate after 24h MPP treatment",
    fill = "Luminescence (RLU)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 12L,
                              face = "bold",
                              hjust = 0.5),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 10L),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 10L)
  )
```

## Answer

There doesn't appear to be any spatial patterns in the data. Wells with higher RLU values seem to be randomly scattered throughout the 1536-well plate.

# Question 2: Which compounds are statistically significantly associated with increased neuronal viability after MPP exposure? Ensure that you check your assumptions.

## Incorporating plate_meta dataset

```{r}
library(dplyr)

# convert plate_meta into long format
cmpd_long <- plate_meta |> 
  pivot_longer(
    # collapse all columns into 1 column except plate_row 
    cols = -plate_row, 
    # all columns collapsed into 1 column named "plate_col"
    names_to = "plate_col", 
    # all RLU values in column named "luminescence"
    values_to = "cmpd"
  )

# Check that pivot_longer() worked
View(cmpd_long)

# Convert plate_row and plate_col values from character to numeric so that cmpd_long 
# can be joined to plate1_long
cmpd_long <- cmpd_long |> 
  mutate(
    # keep numbers after "row"
    plate_row = parse_number(plate_row),
    # keep numbers after "col"
    plate_col = parse_number(plate_col))

# Combine plate1_long and cmpd_long using left_join
combined_data <- plate1_long |> 
  left_join(cmpd_long, 
            by = c("plate_row", "plate_col"))

# Check that left_join() worked
View(cmpd_long)
```

## Tidying combined_data

```{r}
# Replace cmpd column with two new columns for the cmpd number and 
# condition (ctrl/test)
combined_data <- combined_data |> 
  separate(
    cmpd,
    into = c("prefix", "cmpd", "cond"),
    sep = "_"
  ) |> 
  # remove prefix
  select(-prefix)

# Check two new columns contain the cmpd number and the condition type
View(combined_data)

# Check that each compound (test/ctrl) has 4 replicates
combined_data  |> 
  count(cmpd, cond) |> 
  filter(n != 4)
```

## Analyse how average luminescence changes between conditions (test vs. ctrl) for each compound

```{r}
summary <- combined_data |> 
  group_by(cmpd, cond) |> 
  summarise(
    mean_lum = mean(luminescence),
    sd_lum = sd(luminescence),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
    )
# Check summary dataset created includes mean_lum and sd_lum columns
View(summary)

comparison_data <- summary |> 
  select(cmpd, cond, mean_lum) |> 
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = cond,
    values_from = mean_lum
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    difference = test - ctrl,
    percent_change = 100 * (test - ctrl) / ctrl
  )

View(comparison_data)
```

## Assumption 1: Observations are independent of one another

## Assumption 2: Outcome is approximately normally distributed within each group

Install and load "rstatix" package

```{r}
install.packages("rstatix")
library(rstatix)
```

Generate Q-Q plots to accept/reject normality

```{r}
# Determine residuals for each compound and condition from the group's mean
residual_data <- combined_data |>
  group_by(cmpd, cond) |>
  mutate(
    residual = luminescence - mean(luminescence)
  ) |>
  ungroup()

# Check that residual column was added  
View(residual_data)

# Generate Q-Q plots for control compounds and test compounds 
ggplot(residual_data, aes(sample = residual)) +
  geom_qq() +
  geom_qq_line() +
  facet_wrap(~cond) +
  labs(
    title = "Q-Q plots of within-group residuals",
    x = "Theoretical quantiles",
    y = "Residual luminescence (RLU)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
# Assess normality using Shapiro-Wilk tests
shapiro_results <- combined_data |>
  group_by(cmpd, cond) |>
  summarise(
    shapiro_p = shapiro.test(luminescence)$p.value,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

shapiro_results |>
  summarise(
    total_tests = n(),
    p_below_05 = sum(shapiro_p < 0.05),
    percentage = mean(shapiro_p < 0.05) * 100
  )
```

Normality within each group was assessed using Q-Q plots of within-group residuals and Shapiro-Wilk tests. The Q-Q plots for both control and test wells showed points lying close to the reference line, with only minor deviations in the extreme tails. Shapiro-Wilk tests were run separately for each compound and condition (384 groups); 26 (6.8%) had p \< 0.05, which is close to the \~5% expected by chance alone if all groups were normally distributed. Together, these results provide no strong evidence against normality within groups, so the normality assumption was considered reasonable and a parametric t-test was appropriate rather than a non-parametric alternative (Wilcoxon rank-sum test).

## Assumption 3: Equal variance

To assess whether the test and control group have approximately equal population variances for each of the 192 compounds, the *summary* dataset generated earlier can ...

```{r}

variance_check <- summary |>
  select(cmpd, cond, sd_lum) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = cond,
    values_from = sd_lum
  ) |>
  mutate(
    var_ctrl = ctrl^2,
    var_test = test^2,
    variance_ratio = pmax(var_ctrl, var_test) /
      pmin(var_ctrl, var_test)
  )

View(variance_check)

summary(variance_check$variance_ratio)
```

The homogeneity of variance assumption was assessed by comparing sample variances between test and control conditions for each compound. Variance ratios ranged from 1.005 to 91.467, with a median of 2.348, indicating that the observed variances were similar for some compounds but differed substantially for others. Given the variability in these ratios and the uncertainty associated with four technical replicates per condition, equal population variances could not be confidently assumed across all compounds.

## Welch t-test

Following assessment of the statistical assumptions, a one-sided Welch's t-test has been selected to compare luminescence between test and control conditions for each of the 192 compounds. Although Q-Q plots and Shapiro–Wilk tests suggested no widespread severe departures from normality, equal variances between groups cannot be confidently assumed.

```{r}

# Perform a Welch's t-test for each compound

welch_results <- combined_data |>
  # Group data by compound to perform a seperate t-test for each
  group_by(cmpd) |>
  t_test(
    luminescence ~ cond, # Compare luminescence between ctrl/group conditions
    var.equal = FALSE, # Welch's t-test allows for unequal variances
    alternative = "less", # Test whether ctrl RLUs < test RLUs
    p.adjust.method = "none" # Retain unadjusted p-values 
    # Remove grouping before multiple testing correction
  ) |> ungroup() |> 
  # Apply BH correction across all compounds to control for 
  # the false discovery rate from multiple testing 
  adjust_pvalue(method = "BH")
```

```{r}

# Identify compound with statistically significant differences in luminescence 
# following multiple-testing correction

significant_compounds <- welch_results |>
  # Filter for compounds with BH-adjusted p-values < 0.05
  filter(p.adj < 0.05) |>
  # Arrange compounds in ascending order of adjusted p-value
  arrange(p.adj)
```

# Question 3: What are the mechanisms of action and targets of the compounds you identify in Q2?

```{r}
# Join compound_dict to comparison_data to obtain information about
# each compound's biological target and action

# Load stringr package for string manipulation
library(stringr)

# Retain all rows from comparison_data and match cmpd info
comparison_data <- comparison_data |>
  left_join(
    compound_dict |>
      # Remove "cmpd_" prefix from compound IDs to match 
      # the format of the cmpd column in comparison_data 
      mutate(cmpd = str_remove(id, "^cmpd_")) |>
      # Remove original ID column as no longer needed
      select(-id),
    # Match the two datasets using compound identifier
    by = "cmpd"
  )

# Identify the biological targets and mechanism of actions of previously identified significant compounds from Q2
comparison_data |>
  # Retain only compounds identified as significant in Q2
  filter(cmpd %in% significant_compounds$cmpd) |>
  # Display compound ID, taregt enzyme, action and HGNC symbol
  select(cmpd, target_enzyme, action, hgnc_symbol)
  # View the filtered results
  View()
```

All four of the compounds that are statistically significantly associated with increased neuronal viability following MPP exposure are agonists, though act on different enzymes. Compound 4550 targets enzyme 26002 (MOXD1), compound 4635 targets enzyme 6817 (SULT1A1), compound 6314 targets enzyme 4128 (MAOA) and compound 6618 targets enzyme 124907837 (no HGNC symbol).

# Save results

```{r}
# Export results for collaborative analysis
saveRDS(significant_compounds, "hit_targets.rds")
```
